results.evidence: Retry found only round-trip distance and gain figures (1,050-1,100 ft to the saddle; ~600 ft more saddle-to-summit in an Oregon Hikers report; ~1,600 ft total in a hiking guide). No source states a car-to-car descent figure for this route, so loss_ft cannot be changed under the rules. Would settle: an outside source giving the car-to-car elevation loss for Pinnacle Saddle / South Gully.

Sources still split along the same line as the row: SummitPost calls the easiest route 4th class and the standard route a 3rd and 4th class scramble, and an Oregon Hikers report says it turned into Class 3/4 scrambling (both supporting the Class 3-4 / 4th Class pill); a hiking guide and a 2024 WTA trip report call the south gully mostly class 2 with a few class 3 moves (supporting the itinerary and descent text). No source supports low 5th on the standard line, but the split on the maximum class is genuine. Would settle: a route-specific description (e.g. a Mountaineers scramble route page, blocked to fetch here) naming the standard South Gully's grade.

Re-fetched the park climbing page: Winter Self-Registration September 15 - May 21, Summer Walk-Up Registration May 22 - September 30, wilderness peak season May 1 - September 15; the official source itself overlaps in late September. The park's climbing blog shows the self-registration start moves year to year (e.g. a 2023 post announcing it began September 11), so no fixed date settles it. Would settle: the current season's park announcement of when self-registration opens.

Outside sources give ~11,500 ft as the trip total (matching gain_ft and the totalNote) but no per-day gain figures; the itinerary days sum to 12,150 ft. Under the rules no day figure is rebalanced without a source stating it. Would settle: a trip report giving per-day gains for a Longmire - 6,400 ft saddle - 10,700 ft col - summit itinerary.

Retry (Medical Moose Labs, Hebert and Spokalpine trip reports, CascadeClimbers TR listings) found times and pitch counts but no stated car-to-car gain for this route. USGS point elevation at the trailhead pin reads ~5,380 ft; the peak is widely listed at 7,565 ft, so 1,365 ft is clearly too low, but no source states the figure and none may be computed. Would settle: a trip report or route page stating the car-to-car gain.

Sources continue to split by style: Mountain Project 10 pitches, SuperTopo ~12, a Spokalpine party climbed 9 pitches with some simul-climbing, a Medical Moose Labs party broke it into 3 long pitches. No single count has two agreeing independent sources. Would settle: stating it as a range in the pitches-bearing fields, which needs an owner decision on the numeric column.

Spokalpine: summit at 1 PM, back down at 2 PM (~1 hr); Hebert party took roughly 2.5 hrs summit to van (outing 9:30 AM - 3:30 PM). Medical Moose Labs gives no descent time. Sources disagree, so neither descentTimeHrs 1 nor the itinerary's ~2 hrs is established. Would settle: a third report timing summit-to-car.

results.fact: Nearest hospital (Skagit Valley Hospital, Mount Vernon)
results.evidence: The stated '75 miles west (90 minute drive)' is inconsistent with the row's own 3-3.5 hr drive from Seattle (Mount Vernon lies on that drive), and PeaceHealth United General in Sedro-Woolley is closer on the west side; east-side options are Mid-Valley (Omak) and Three Rivers (Brewster). A Methow Valley News article says a Washington Pass accident victim is 90 minutes to two hours by ambulance from the nearest hospital without naming it. Would settle: routed drive distances from the hairpin to Sedro-Woolley, Omak and Brewster from two sources.

results.fact: Summit elevation (waypoint elev / high_point_ft 7,840 vs published 7,565)
results.evidence: SummitPost and a 2007 CascadeClimbers trip report title both give Poster Peak as 7,565 ft (an unnamed map point), while the row's summit waypoint and high_point_ft say 7,840. A USGS elevation grid around the summit pin shows the pin itself at ~7,440 ft but terrain reaching ~7,830 ft about 0.8 km SE, so it is unclear whether 7,840 describes a different, higher point on the ridge. Would settle: a peakbagger/listsofjohn page (blocked here) placing Poster Peak's summit coordinate and elevation.
